reason_for_supersession: That node's boundary-pinning diagnostic only caught the 'hard' pinning shape (t0~0 AND tau~its lower bound of 1ms), reporting 20.8% of gate-passing cells pinned and calling S+ 'essentially clean' (1/38, 2.6%). Manually inspecting one flagged S+ cell (V3a/d, group mean 11.9ms) found a second shape entirely missed by that definition: 4/6 sessions had t0~0 but with tau spread across the FULL range up to its 150ms upper bound, not pinned low -- i.e. a slow, already-in-progress ramp compressed against the t0=0 causality wall, not a fast degenerate step. scripts/diagnose_onset_hierarchy_boundary_pinning.py was revised the same day to flag t0<1ms regardless of tau (subdivided hard/soft for interpretability, pooled for the headline number since both are equally untrustworthy as onset estimates).

by_class.S+: 15/43 (34.9%) pinned -- worse than first reported, but a real clean majority (65.1%) remains, concentrated in specific areas

clean_only_rerun.method: scripts/rehierarchy_test_clean_onsets_only.py -- reuses fit_class_onset_latency.py's own bootstrap_area_class/hierarchy_test functions unmodified (imported, not reimplemented), restricted to cells with t0>=1ms in addition to the pipeline's existing r2>=0.3/converged gate. Neither jnwb/onset_fitting.py nor scripts/fit_class_onset_latency.py were edited.

result.omnibus: 0 areas survive MIN_SESSIONS_PER_CELL=3 on the clean subset -- insufficient_data

S+.verdict: H3_superposition_candidate (p_holm >= 0.05, but this is a 5-area exact permutation test with a large effect size, not a flat null -- see interpretation below)

interpretation: Once artifact-pinned sessions are excluded, only S+ retains enough clean data to test at all (5 of 10 areas), and its onset ordering is nearly monotonic with the bottom-up hierarchy (V2 earliest, TEO latest, one adjacent swap at FEF/TEO) -- the opposite qualitative read from the contaminated full-data result, which looked flat (rho=0.07). This is suggestive of H1 (feedforward-consistent visual response propagation) rather than H3 (superposition/volume-conduction-like), but is NOT a significant result (p=0.081) and rests on only 5 areas with 3-7 sessions each -- underpowered to confirm, not to be reported as a finding. omnibus/S-/O+/O- currently cannot be tested at all on artifact-free data; this is a real data-volume ceiling (more sessions/units), not something the fitting method itself can fix.
recommendation: Do not report the pre-correction H3-superposition verdict for omnibus or S+ anymore -- it was built substantially from pinned cells. Do not yet report the clean-only S+ H1-leaning result as a finding either -- it is promising and worth pursuing (e.g. more sessions, or a wider pre-onset fit window that lets the model represent a pre-existing ramp instead of clipping it, which would recover some of the 15 excluded S+ cells rather than discarding them). O+/O-/S- need substantially more sessions/units before any per-area onset comparison is possible for those classes, independent of the pinning issue.
